page: Microsoft Azure M32bs_v3 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the MBSMediumMemoryv3 family. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical Intel Xeon 8473C cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 4.0 GHz. The processor includes a 105 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, relying instead on external block storage with Premium Storage capabilities.

In benchmark evaluations, the M32bs_v3 demonstrates strong performance characteristics. It achieves top-tier results in Geekbench single-core testing and high-speed text generation for small LLM models (135M). Multi-threaded operations, such as bzip3 decompression and static web serving throughput, also rank in the top 25% tier. However, the server exhibits a performance tradeoff in large-scale workloads, as evidenced by a weak rating in text generation for large 70B LLM models. Memory bandwidth tests show 2764.98 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 182.67 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the M32bs_v3 offers a balanced profile for memory-intensive workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. The dedicated CPU allocation and high clock speed make it suitable for memory-optimized applications, database operations, software compilation, and medium-scale text processing. It is well-suited for enterprise applications, caching layers, and web serving environments requiring a high memory-to-vCPU ratio.
